title: Applied ML — weekly sprint wrap and experiment digest (2026-06-02)
content:
Sprint goal recap:
- Finish baseline PTQ experiments for Llama-2 13B variants.
- Ship a lightweight eval harness for instruction-following regressions.
- Lock initial onboarding checklist for Mistral-7B adapter.

Attendees (sync 2026-06-02): Priya (owner), Ethan, Sofia, Liam, Noor (SRE), Camille (infra). Quick notes below, messy — meant to capture decisions, numbers, and open questions.

High-level summary:
- Quantization: PTQ 4-bit (nf4) gave ~1.9x throughput on A100 L4, ~2.3x on T4-hosted tests, with modest quality drop on open-book QA tests (exact deltas below). QAT probe for 4-bit was started on a tiny subset — early signs it recovers ~60% of the RL accuracy loss but is expensive to run.
- Evals: New instruction-following harness (v0.1) runs streaming comparisons between model variants; we detected a regression vs baseline in safety rejection for one prompt family.
- Onboarding: Mistral-7B adapter checklist ready for initial private deployment; still need KMS policy signoff and config for prefix cache warmup.

Experiment logs (quick digest):
1) PTQ 4-bit (nf4) on Llama-2-13B (fp16 baseline):
   - Setup: transformer-ops branch + quant-kit v1.4; calibration on 8k tokens of mixed-domain text.
   - Perf (p95 token latency, batch=1, seq=512):
     - fp16 baseline: 57 ms p95 (A100-L4)
     - 4-bit nf4: 31 ms p95 (A100-L4)
     - T4 (4-bit): 78 ms p95 (T4-capped) vs 180 ms fp16
   - Throughput (tokens/s, batch=8):
     - fp16: 120 t/s
     - 4-bit: 230 t/s
   - Quality (held-out instr-follow tests, 1k prompts):
     - instruction-accuracy: baseline 92.4% -> 4-bit 89.1% (delta -3.3 pts)
     - safety-reject rate: baseline 5% -> 4-bit 7.2% (increase on a particular class of prompts)
   - Notes: regression concentrated on long-context retrieval prompts where kv-cache indexing happened more frequently. Hypothesis: per-layer rounding interacts with rotary scaling causing subtle drift on retrieval embeddings.

2) QAT probe (toy run):
   - 200 steps of QAT on adapter weights only (low LR).
   - Recovered ~60% of the instruction-accuracy gap, safety-reject returned near baseline on the toy set.
   - Cost: ~6 GPU-hours for small run (not yet scaled). Action: decide whether to run full QAT vs targeted layer quantization.

3) Eval harness v0.1 (instruction/regression):
   - Components: prompt mutator, reference oracle, diffs recorder, streaming comparator.
   - Found a reproducible regression for prompts that use explicit JSON schema enforcement; 4-bit model emits slightly malformed JSON in ~2.4% of cases (baseline 0.6%).
   - Linked CI: internal:/evals/weekly/run-2026-06-01 (see linked_artifacts).

Onboarding checklist: Mistral-7B adapter (initial private test)
- Completed: model pull + signature verification, small inference smoke tests, adapter packaging, packaging docs.
- Remaining: KMS policy approval (security), HSM rotation policy + documented key IDs, console route for customer to pin to adapter build.
- Observability: need to add per-request token-cost header in private control plane for adapter tests (capture early).

Operational / infra notes:
- KV-cache warmup: Camille outlined a warmup script that replays top-500 recent prefixes to prepopulate caches in dedicated pools. Plan: run warmup before canary rollout for the adapter.
- Autoscaling: Noor flagged that our current scaling policy underestimates bursty token streams; proposed tweak: lower p95 latency target for scale-up decision to avoid queueing.

Decisions made in sync:
- Run a single medium-cost QAT job targeted to the top 6 layers + embedding matrices for Llama-2-13B (Ethan to own). Budget approved: ~48 GPU-hours on dedicated infra.
- Break out a focused eval suite for JSON-schema prompts to add to pre-deploy checks (Sofia to own).
- Hold Mistral-7B adapter private rollout until KMS signoff (security), timeline: target week of 2026-06-08.

Action items (owner, eta):
- Ethan: kick off targeted QAT job (top-6 layers), track perf + quality, report by 2026-06-09.
- Sofia: add JSON-schema prompt tests to harness, integrate into presubmit, PR by 2026-06-05.
- Liam: add metric series for safety-reject-by-prompt-family to console (short-term dashboard card), ETA 2026-06-07.
- Camille: implement kv-cache warmup script + docs, PR for runbook 2026-06-06.
- Priya: draft short postmortem of the observed retrieval regression and circulate w/ research + infra by 2026-06-08.

Blockers / open questions:
- Is the safety-reject regression clinically significant for customers? Need product input on acceptable delta thresholds. (Ping product-hosted-api)
- QAT cost vs benefit: if QAT recovers only ~60% of gap it may not be worth the 10x runtime cost for all models. Suggest we explore mixed-precision hybrids or selective layer FP16 retention.
- KV-cache correctness: do we have a deterministic repro for the index misalignment? Early repros are flaky. Liam to instrument cache indices in the runtime debug build.

Quick follow-ups / notes-to-self:
- Keep experiment seeds and calibration datasets versioned under /datasets/quant-cal/ (Ethan will upload).
- Add a simple README to the eval harness explaining prompt mutator semantics and how to add new prompt families.
- Save a copy of the JSON-schema failure examples to the safety folder for review by the safety team.

Meeting artifacts and links: see linked_artifacts above. Also: internal slack thread #applied-ml-quant for ad-hoc discussion.

Low-effort wins for next sprint (prioritized):
1) Add schema/formatting checks to presubmit (low cost, high value).
2) Run targeted QAT on a small subset of customer-critical prompts to measure real-world delta.
3) Implement cache warmup as part of the adapter rollout checklist.

Notes: this doc is intentionally concise and a bit rough — it's the sprint-wrap for the research lane. If you want more raw logs (per-step metrics, full eval dumps), see internal:/evals/weekly/run-2026-06-01 or request the raw buckets from Ethan.


TODO (short list):
- [ ] Product decision: accept safety delta threshold for 4-bit? (action: product-hosted-api)
- [ ] Security: KMS signoff for adapter keys (action: security).
- [ ] Infra: run warmup + validate cache correctness after warmup.

End of notes.
